audit.report: Checkout success dropped to 0% for 30 seconds with $18,400/min revenue at risk after a poisoned session text triggered lock contention. The root blocker was pid 92535 running batch_replayable_month_end_close (inventory_month_end_close), idle in transaction for 4.9 seconds, blocking 12 sessions. Both guardians agreed terminating the blocker would cost a 95-minute replay but waiting would cost ~$1.1M in lost revenue, far exceeding the 60-second degradation tolerance. An active change calendar (CHG-4410) with consult_owner policy required human escalation to finance-ops. The incident ended with escalation after 130 seconds; no automated action was executed.
audit.root_cause: A poisoned session text injected into the database caused lock contention where batch_replayable_month_end_close (pid 92535) held locks idle in transaction, blocking all checkout sessions.
lessons: Pre-register batch_replayable_month_end_close (inventory_month_end_close) in the change calendar with an explicit emergency termination policy to bypass consult_owner delays during checkout outages.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian proposed terminate in R1 with strong evidence but missed the mandatory change calendar check (invariant I2), forcing a revision. The Continuity Guardian correctly enforced the invariant but the escalation path added 130 seconds of 0% checkout before human intervention.
follow_ups: Finance-ops owner to confirm termination authority for inventory_month_end_close during checkout emergencies and update CHG-4410 policy from consult_owner to auto_terminate_if_checkout_down.
Engineering to implement idle-in-transaction watchdog for batch_replayable workloads with < 5s threshold when checkout SLO breached.
Security to analyze poisoned session text injection vector and deploy input sanitization at the application gateway.
